statement: Hold a complete building model (rooms, faces, apertures, doors, shades) as a single typed model object that the plugin can pass to simulations.

source.ref: PO_Model / PO_Room / PO_Face / PO_Aperture / PO_Door / PO_Shade

superiority: One native building-model type that is the same object used for geometry, simulation and export, with no conversion step between model views.

acceptance.corpus: Model with 20 rooms, 100 apertures, 15 shades
acceptance.tolerance: Object counts and total areas preserved through build, save and reload; area differences < 1e-9

statement: Define daylight sensor grids and camera views as part of the model for daylight and view simulations.
superiority: Sensor grids placed and edited directly on room geometry with live count and spacing readout.

acceptance.corpus: Room 6 m by 8 m, 0.5 m grid at 0.8 m height; 4 views at standard fisheye
acceptance.tolerance: Sensor count equals floor-cell count; positions at 0.8 m +/- 1e-6

statement: Create and assign opaque constructions, construction sets and materials, and window glazing, with thermal properties.
superiority: Material library with computed U-value and R-value feedback and unit-checked editing.

acceptance.corpus: Wall assembly of 4 layers with known conductivity; ASHRAE handbook U-factor example
acceptance.tolerance: Computed U-factor within 0.5 percent of hand calculation

statement: Define radiance modifiers and modifier sets to describe surface optical properties such as reflectance and transmittance for daylight simulations.
superiority: Optical material editor with preview and automatic validation of energy conservation (reflectance plus transmittance at most 1).

acceptance.corpus: 10 modifiers incl. plastic, glass and trans types
acceptance.tolerance: Reflectance sums validated; invalid modifier values rejected 100 percent of the time

statement: Define program types and schedules (occupancy, lighting, equipment, setpoints) for energy models.
superiority: Schedule editor that previews annual patterns and checks fractional range and totals.

acceptance.corpus: Office program with weekday/weekend/holiday schedules
acceptance.tolerance: Equivalent full-load hours equal analytic sum within 0.01 hour

statement: Prepare a simulation run by loading a recipe (a packaged simulation workflow) and binding its inputs to the model and weather.
superiority: Recipes defined as typed local workflows with versioning and input validation before dispatch.

acceptance.corpus: Recipe such as annual daylight with model and weather inputs
acceptance.tolerance: Missing or wrongly typed inputs flagged before submission 100 percent; run configuration identical on repeat

statement: Check recipe inputs are complete and valid before a run is submitted.
superiority: Static input validator that checks units, file existence and model validity before any compute is spent.

acceptance.corpus: 10 runs with seeded input errors (missing EPW, bad grid)
acceptance.tolerance: All 10 errors reported with the specific input name

statement: Attach user data (run names, model metadata such as window-to-wall ratio) to a run so results can be filtered and compared later.
superiority: Metadata is automatically harvested from slider and parameter values so every run is self-describing.

acceptance.corpus: Study of 20 runs with 3 variable parameters
acceptance.tolerance: Every run record carries the 3 parameter values; query by parameter returns exact set

statement: Schedule a study of one or many runs on the cloud or the local machine and return a handle to follow it.
superiority: Local-first scheduler that parallelises many runs across all cores and optional cloud workers with identical results and resumable progress.

acceptance.corpus: Study of 50 daylight-factor runs of varied window sizes
acceptance.tolerance: Results from local and cloud workers equal within 1e-6; 50-run study completes with linear speedup to 8 cores

statement: Follow a study and list previous studies, with status counts for queued, running, succeeded and failed runs.
superiority: Live status feed with per-run progress, logs and re-run of failed runs only.

acceptance.corpus: Study of 30 runs with 3 seeded failures
acceptance.tolerance: Counts reported exactly: 27 succeeded, 3 failed; re-run only 3 failed

statement: Inspect the outputs of a completed run and load result assets into Grasshopper, from the cloud or from files already on disk.

source.ref: Check Run Results / List Run Assets / Load Assets

superiority: Lazy loading of large result files with columnar access and built-in visualisation.

acceptance.corpus: Annual daylight run result with 5000 sensors x 8760 hours
acceptance.tolerance: Loaded values equal result file exactly; load time for one sensor column < 100 ms

statement: Create and fetch cloud projects and list their assets to organise study data.

source.ref: Add a project / Get a project / List Project Assets

superiority: Projects map to local folders with transparent sync and ACL.

acceptance.corpus: Create project, list assets before and after upload
acceptance.tolerance: Asset list changes by exactly the uploaded set

statement: Upload local files and folders (models, weather files) into a cloud project as assets for studies.
superiority: Resumable chunked uploads with content-hash de-duplication so unchanged files are never re-sent.

acceptance.corpus: Upload 20 files totalling 200 MB; re-upload with 1 changed file
acceptance.tolerance: Second upload sends only changed file bytes; hashes match remote

statement: Authenticate with the cloud service from within the design environment using an interactive login or an API key.
superiority: Single sign-on with keychain storage that never writes a key into a saved definition.

acceptance.corpus: Login flow with expired token and revoked key
acceptance.tolerance: Expired token triggers refresh; revoked key refused; saved file contains no credential string

statement: Run parametric design iterations by recording the outputs of every slider and value-list combination, with data and images saved to disk.
superiority: Native parameter-sweep runner with resumable progress, deduplication of repeated points and an in-app results table.

acceptance.corpus: 3 sliders with 5 values each (125 iterations)
acceptance.tolerance: All 125 combinations recorded once; data file has 125 rows; restart resumes from last completed row

statement: Export a building model to external energy-modelling formats for exchange with other design and analysis tools.
superiority: Round-trip tested exporters with validation of geometry and a diff report of dropped properties.

acceptance.corpus: Sample model with 10 rooms exported to each format and re-imported where possible
acceptance.tolerance: Total floor area of exported file equals model within 0.1 percent; no unreported property loss

statement: Read a building model from interchange formats and ensure no loss of geometry, zoning, constructions, schedules and HVAC when moving to and from the simulation tool chain.
superiority: Lossless native import and export of the open building-model JSON format with a published schema and round-trip tests.

acceptance.corpus: Public HBJSON sample models (Ladybug Tools sample files)
acceptance.tolerance: Round-trip preserves room, face, aperture counts and areas within 1e-6 and all property keys

statement: Edit and repair a building model: fix gaps, snap to grid, merge small rooms, simplify windows and curved edges, split core and perimeter zones, add plenums, and validate.
superiority: Interactive validation that fixes gaps and misalignments in real time with preview and undo for each repair.

acceptance.corpus: Imported plan with 30 rooms, 2 percent area in gaps/overlaps, 5 tiny rooms
acceptance.tolerance: After repair, 0 validation errors; total floor area change < 0.5 percent; every repair undoable

statement: Run an annual energy simulation recipe for a building model with weather and design-day files and load the results.

source.ref: Rhino plugin: Run Simulation and Load Results (annual-energy-use recipe)

superiority: Local EnergyPlus-class engine with the same recipe interface, no cloud dependency, deterministic and reproducible results.

acceptance.corpus: ASHRAE 140 BESTEST case 600 with TMY weather
acceptance.tolerance: Annual heating and cooling within the ASHRAE 140 reference range for case 600

statement: Schedule studies programmatically through an API: create a job with owner, project and recipe, upload inputs, create one run per input set, poll status and download outputs.
superiority: Scripting API on the app that submits studies locally or to workers with a stable, typed client.

acceptance.corpus: Batch of 10 models submitted through the API script
acceptance.tolerance: 10 runs created; all statuses reach terminal state; outputs downloaded for all successes

statement: Build and deploy web apps that create studies, check status, chart results and visualise them in a viewer or in the modelling environment.
superiority: Embedded result viewer and app builder that works with local data without cloud deployment.

acceptance.corpus: App that creates a study and plots a result chart
acceptance.tolerance: App renders chart values equal to downloaded output; no cloud credential required for local mode
